detail: `loginWithPassword` and `verifyMfaCode` from `auth-email-password/static-login` now use `postJson` from `auth-email-password/static-client` and answer as before; a signed-in visitor's CSRF cookie is now sent along. `requestPasswordReset`, `resetPassword`, `requestEmailVerification`, `verifyEmail`, `requestAccountUnlock`, `confirmAccountUnlock`, `requestSignup` and `confirmSignup` from the web auth client no longer throw when the network fails; they return `{ ok: false, error: { reason: "network" } }`. A 401 without an error code now gives the reason `unauthenticated`, and a token rejected only by the schema gives `malformed_token`. `static-login` no longer exports `STATIC_NETWORK_FAILURE_REASON` and `STATIC_RATE_LIMITED_REASON`.
migration: Import `STATIC_NETWORK_REASON` and `STATIC_RATE_LIMITED_REASON` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/auth-email-password/static-client` instead; the values are the same (`"network"`, `"rate_limited"`).

title: Default auth pages cover every auth path and take a shell
detail: `emailPasswordClient({ defaultAuthPages })` now takes `false` or `{ paths?: Partial<AuthPaths> }`; `true` is no longer accepted. Besides forgot-password, reset-password and unlock-account, signed-out visitors now get `/signup` (only when the server registers the signup status query; a visitor with a session cookie passes through), `/signup/complete`, `/verify-email` and `/invite/accept`, each at the path from `paths`, resolved like the server's `auth.mail.paths`. Login links on these pages point to `/login` under the app base path. The new option `authShell` wraps every auth card through `AuthShellProvider`.
migration: Replace `defaultAuthPages: true` with no option. Apps that pass custom `auth.mail.paths` to the server pass the same object as `defaultAuthPages: { paths }`. Delete app gates that only mounted these screens, and pass the shell as `authShell` instead of wrapping `AuthShellProvider` in an own gate. Keep an own earlier gate only for screens that need app-specific props.

title: mountStaticLoginForm binds the static login to a data-attribute markup contract

Token request handlers no longer return the token
detail: `request-password-reset`, `request-email-verification` and `request-account-unlock` now return only `{ kind }`, and `signup-request` returns only `kind` and `expiresAt`. The result of the three token request handlers is the same for every address, known or not, so `kind: "no-op"` no longer occurs there. The token reaches the user only by mail.
migration: Code that read `token` or `email` from the result of these handlers gets the token from the sent mail instead. Checks for `kind: "no-op"` on reset, verification and unlock requests are removed. The types `TokenRequestSuccess` and `TokenRequestNoOp` no longer exist; `TokenRequestData<K>` is `{ readonly kind: K }`.

How to send an auth mail after the render*Email helpers were removed in 0.363.0
migration:
App code that rendered an auth mail itself and passed the result as `data`, for example `notify("auth-email-password:signup-activation", { route: { email }, data: renderActivationEmail({ url, expiresAt, locale, appName }), priority: "critical" })`, breaks twice since 0.363.0: the helper is gone and the notification type is now `auth-email-password:notify:signup-activation`. The stored template renders subject and body; the app only passes template variables.
For a signup activation link, call `issueSignupActivation({ redis, notify: ctx.notify, email, appUrl, appName, locale, timeZone, tokenTtlMinutes, onTokenStored })` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/auth-email-password` (only redis, notify, email and appUrl are required). It drops any live signup token for the email, stores a new one under the keys signup-confirm reads and sends the mail. `appUrl` is the bare activation page; a function `(locale) => url` picks the page per locale.
If the app stores the token itself and only needs the mail, call `ctx.notify(AuthMailNotificationTypes.signupActivation, { route: { email }, data: { appName, actionUrl, validFor, validUntil }, locale, priority: "critical" })`. `AuthMailNotificationTypes` comes from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/auth-email-password`. All four variables are required strings: ctx.notify checks them against the declared template variables and throws an InternalError on a missing or invalid one, which fails the write. `actionUrl` is the page URL with `token=<encodeURIComponent(token)>` appended as a query parameter and must be an http, https or mailto URL. `validFor` and `validUntil` come from `tokenMailExpiry({ expiresAt, issuedAt, timeZone }, locale)` in `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/auth-email-password/email-templates`. Only send a `locale` that has a template for the type, because the renderer has no locale fallback and a locale without a template sends nothing: use `resolveMailLocale(locale)` when `hasMailTranslationKey(resolveMailLocale(locale), "auth.mail.activation.subject")` is true (both from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/i18n`), otherwise `"en"`. The other mails use the subject keys `auth.mail.reset.subject`, `auth.mail.unlock.subject`, `auth.mail.verify.subject` and `auth.mail.invite.subject`.
The other auth mails work the same way with `AuthMailNotificationTypes.passwordReset`, `.accountUnlock`, `.emailVerification` and `.invite`; the invite mail also needs a `role` variable.

detail: The sections-based content type only fed the retired renderer-simple. Auth mails are template notifications with variables, so nothing builds or consumes AuthMailContent anymore.
migration: Drop AuthMailContent imports; the auth mail text lives in the seeded templates and is overridden per tenant in the template editor.

title: Auth mails are notifications with seeded templates, render*Email is gone
detail: password-reset, account-unlock, email-verification, signup-activation and invite are declared as r.notification with a localized template and variables, seeded as system templates at boot and rendered by renderer-mail-html, so a tenant can override the text in the template editor. A locale without its own subject key falls back to en, because the renderer has no locale fallback. AuthMailNotificationTypes is exported for the qualified names.
migration: The notification types are now `auth-email-password:notify:<name>` (before: the plain names). Update delivery preferences, preference rows and tests that reference the old names. renderResetPasswordEmail, renderUnlockAccountEmail, renderVerifyEmail, renderActivationEmail, renderInviteEmail, AuthMailSection, RenderTokenContentArgs and RenderInviteEmailArgs are removed; AuthMailContent stays. An app that mounts auth-email-password now needs template-resolver, renderer-foundation and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-mail-html (composeRendererStack() from dev-server mounts all of them; with includeBundled, composeFeatures adds whichever is missing). Boot fails with a clear error otherwise, and apps without the template tables need a schema migration (`kumiko schema generate`). kumiko-schema-check counts the three as implicit features of every HAS_AUTH app, so its check fails until that migration exists. Tests that read the token from a mail use the text part (`mail.text`); the html part encodes `=` as `=`.

title: auth handlers switch from GUEST_USER (roles: ["all"]) to the anonymous identity with a per-IP rateLimit
migration: The auth-email-password and auth-mfa handlers reachable from unauthenticated /auth/* routes (login, invite-accept-with-login, invite-signup-complete, reset-password, signup-confirm, verify-email, confirm-account-unlock, signup-request, the token-request handlers, mfa verify, mfa enable-start-preauth, mfa enable-confirm-preauth) now declare access: { roles: ["anonymous"] } instead of access: { roles: ["all"] }, each with its own rateLimit: { per: "ip+handler", limit, windowSeconds }. Enforcing that rateLimit on a request that carries a client IP requires a RateLimitResolver (Redis), same as the already rate-limited self-registration-status query; without one these handlers fail with InternalError (fail-closed, #1467). The password-reset, email-verification and account-unlock request routes keep answering 200 for anti-enumeration, so there the failure shows up as a "[kumiko] token request handler ... failed" error log line and no mail is sent. Wire Redis (or context.rateLimit) before relying on these routes. Test fixtures that hand-roll a guest SessionUser with roles: ["all"] must switch to roles: ["anonymous"] (or createAnonymousUser from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine).
